# Offset-encoding density benchmark

**Generated file - do not edit by hand.** Regenerate with `bin/offset-encoding-density-report.sh`
(`bin/offset-encoding-density-report.sh --check` fails if this file is stale).

## What this is

PC commits its incomplete-offset map as a **string** in the Kafka offset metadata field, capped at
`OffsetMapCodecManager.DefaultMaxMetadataSize` = 4,096 chars, with back-pressure engaging at 0.75 of that
(`PartitionStateManager.USED_PAYLOAD_THRESHOLD_MULTIPLIER_DEFAULT`) = **3,072 chars**. Past the cap the
payload is dropped and the partition blocks, so density near the cap is direct headroom.

[astubbs#192](https://github.com/astubbs/parallel-consumer/issues/192) (mirror of
[confluentinc#903](https://github.com/confluentinc/parallel-consumer/issues/903)) asks why PC uses
custom run-length/bitset encoders rather than RoaringBitmap, and Base64 rather than something
denser. Nobody had ever measured either alternative. This file is the measurement, and it is
generated by `OffsetEncodingDensityBenchmarkTest` so it cannot drift from the code it describes.

It measures **size only** - there is no JMH and no timing here. Encoded size is a deterministic
function of the incompletes distribution and the range length, which is what makes these numbers
committable. Encode-time CPU is a separate concern owned elsewhere.

## Method

- **Incumbents** are measured through the real `OffsetSimultaneousEncoder.invoke()`, reading
  `getEncodingMap()` (not `sortedEncodings` - that `TreeSet` silently drops size-ties).
- **Candidates** are minimal layout writers inside the test, not registered encoders: real bytes in
  the shape the plan's HTD describes, put through the same `zstd` and the same string arithmetic as
  the incumbents. Nothing here has a decode path, and none of it is production code.
- **Packed bytes** always include the 1-byte magic prefix, so incumbents and candidates are
  compared on the same footing. Every candidate layout begins
  `[magic:1][rangeLength:int4]`, because the incompletes alone cannot reconstruct the top of the
  range (the highest offset is always complete).
- **String length** models the writer's floored rule (KTD6): Base64 `4*ceil(n/3)` for payloads
  below 22 bytes, and the shorter of that and sentinel+Z85 `1 + 5*floor(n/4) + (n%4 ? n%4+1 : 0)`
  - from 22 bytes up always Z85 - beyond it. Both are reported for the winner. No codec is
  implemented here; this is the arithmetic only.
- **Two compression views.** *Forced* sets `OffsetSimultaneousEncoder.compressionForced`, so every
  encoder gets a zstd twin - it shows what compression is worth in principle. *Production* applies
  the real rule, which is now PER ENCODER (KTD8): an encoding gets a zstd twin exactly when its own
  plain form is at or over 200 bytes. Before KTD8 the gate was all-or-nothing - NO twin registered
  for anything if ANY ONE encoder's plain form was under the threshold - which is what R11 required
  fixing before a candidate could ship, and which incumbents and candidates alike are now measured
  under. **The verdicts use the production view.**
- **`ByteArray` is absent** from the tables: `addByteBufferEncoder()` is not called in production,
  as BitSet always beats it.
- **Scenario data is seeded** (`java.util.Random`, seed derived from the family and range size
  only), so this file is byte-identical across runs and across machines.
- **The distributions are assumed, not observed.** No workload telemetry of
  `ratioMetadataSpaceUsedDistributionSummary` is available to this project, so the corpus is the
  plan's best guess at realistic shapes plus two adversarial ones. Read the verdicts with that in
  mind.

### The scenario corpus

| Scenario | Incomplete offsets are |
|---|---|
| `trailing-incomplete-run` | one contiguous run covering the last 5% of the range - the healthy steady state, work in flight at the tail |
| `uniform-random 0.1% / 1% / 5% / 20%` | that fraction of the range, uniformly at random - scattered slow records |
| `clustered-bursts` | bursts of 10-100 consecutive offsets, one burst per 1,000 offsets, at random starts - a few slow keys |
| `alternating-xo` | every other offset - the pathological case for run-length |
| `all-incomplete` | every offset in the range - nothing has succeeded yet |

## Back-pressure engagement points

Where each scenario family's winning payload crosses the 3,072-char back-pressure threshold. This is the
number that says how much headroom the current pipeline actually has, and it is what any density
change has to be judged against.

**Method and its limits:** binary search over a geometric grid of range sizes (x1.2 from 1,000 to 200,000),
evaluating the production-view winner at each probe. The search assumes string length grows
monotonically with range size for a fixed family - true in shape, but not exactly, since zstd is
not monotone in its input and the winning encoder can switch. **So the crossing is located to
within one grid step, not exactly**, and both sides of it are shown. The grid is capped because
each probe costs a full per-offset encode pass; families that never block within the cap say so.

| Scenario | Last fitting range | incompletes | winner | chars | First blocking range | incompletes | winner | chars |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `trailing-incomplete-run` | 197,850 | 9,892 | `RunLengthV2` | 20 | none at or below 197,850 | - | - | - |
| `uniform-random 0.1%` | 197,850 | 198 | `delta-list` | 474 | none at or below 197,850 | - | - | - |
| `uniform-random 1%` | 197,850 | 1,979 | `delta-list+zstd` | 2,869 | none at or below 197,850 | - | - | - |
| `uniform-random 5%` | 55,217 | 2,761 | `delta-list+zstd` | 2,600 | 66,260 | 3,313 | `delta-list+zstd` | 3,099 |
| `uniform-random 20%` | 22,190 | 4,438 | `BitSetCompressed` | 2,635 | 26,628 | 5,326 | `BitSetCompressed` | 3,153 |
| `clustered-bursts` | 197,850 | 10,741 | `RunLengthCompressed` | 783 | none at or below 197,850 | - | - | - |
| `alternating-xo` | 197,850 | 98,925 | `BitSetV2Compressed` | 31 | none at or below 197,850 | - | - | - |
| `all-incomplete` | 197,850 | 197,850 | `RunLengthV2` | 8 | none at or below 197,850 | - | - | - |

The deferred follow-up in the plan - exposing the broker's configurable
`offset.metadata.max.bytes` as a PC option - is sized directly by this table: raising the cap
multiplies every "first blocking range" above, with no wire-format change at all.

## What the numbers say

- **`chunked-bitset`**: best result anywhere in the corpus is **+29.3%** against the incumbent, on uniform-random 0.1% @ range
  10,000 (41 chars vs 58) - but that is a `!` row, where at least one incumbent was too small to earn a zstd twin, so read the margin against the forced table too. It is the production-view winner on **1 of 32** scenarios.
- **`delta-list`**: best result anywhere in the corpus is **+56.4%** against the incumbent, on uniform-random 5% @ range
  1,000 (71 chars vs 163) - but that is a `!` row, where at least one incumbent was too small to earn a zstd twin, so read the margin against the forced table too. It is the production-view winner on **12 of 32** scenarios.
- **`u-run-length`**: best result anywhere in the corpus is **+10.4%** against the incumbent, on uniform-random 5% @ range
  1,000 (146 chars vs 163) - but that is a `!` row, where at least one incumbent was too small to earn a zstd twin, so read the margin against the forced table too. It is the production-view winner on **0 of 32** scenarios.
- **zstd on a sparse bitmap is the incumbent's strongest move.** A BitSet of a low-density
  incompletes set is a long run of zeros with a few ones, and zstd takes it close to its entropy -
  which is why the pre-compression size advantage of a sparse format shrinks so much by the time it
  reaches the string. Compare the plain and zstd candidate columns to see how much of each
  candidate's apparent advantage survives compression.
- **A delta list still beats it on the sparse-to-mid uniform families**, because it encodes the same
  information in ~1 byte per incomplete instead of 1 bit per OFFSET, and zstd then works on a much
  smaller input. The advantage reverses as density rises: at 20% the gaps are short and numerous, so
  one bit per offset is the cheaper representation again.
- **The run-length families are already optimal and nothing here improves them.** For a trailing
  incomplete run, or an all-incomplete range, `RunLength` commits 4-20 chars - a candidate cannot
  beat that, and the 5-byte `[magic:1][rangeLength:int4]` header the candidates carry (against the
  incumbents' 1 byte, since their payloads already imply the range) is decisive at that size.
- **The all-or-nothing compression gate cost real chars, and no longer exists.** It suppressed every
  encoder's zstd twin as soon as one encoding was small; the `alternating-xo` rows were the clearest
  case, where a tiny run-length encoding cost the bitsets a compression that takes them from
  thousands of bytes to a few dozen. KTD8/R11 replaced it with the per-encoder rule these tables are
  now generated under, and that change is independent of any candidate.
- **Base64 vs Z85 is a small win, and it is free.** Z85 converges on ~6% shorter, applies to every
  encoding at once, and is independent of everything else in this report - compare the last two
  columns of either table.

## Verdicts (KTD5)

The rule, restated: a candidate ships only if, post-compression and post-string-encoding under the
production compression rule, it beats the best incumbent by at least **10%** on at least one
scenario class whose incumbent payload is already **at or above 3,072 chars** - so the win is real
headroom where density matters, not a percentage on a payload of a few dozen bytes. At most the
best candidate ships. A measured case-against is a result, not a failure: it is the answer to
astubbs#192.

```
VERDICT chunked-bitset: case-against - best result across the 6 scenario(s) at or above the 3,072-char threshold was uniform-random 20% @ range 100,000: 11,550 chars vs the incumbent's 11,553 (BitSetV2Compressed) - +0.03%, short of the required 10% (delta-list ships instead)
```

```
VERDICT delta-list: ship - best incumbent 58,783 chars -> 45,421 chars on uniform-random 5% @ range 1,000,000 (delta-list+zstd), 22.73% denser; clears the 10% bar on a payload already at or above the 3,072-char back-pressure threshold
```

```
VERDICT u-run-length: case-against - best result across the 6 scenario(s) at or above the 3,072-char threshold was clustered-bursts @ range 1,000,000: 3,579 chars vs the incumbent's 3,574 (RunLengthCompressed) - -0.14%, short of the required 10% (delta-list ships instead)
```

### The scenarios the rule was decided on

Every row whose incumbent payload is at or above the threshold - so the whole input to the rule
above is visible and can be checked against the tables. `cap x` is the incumbent payload as a
multiple of the 4,096-char metadata cap.

| Scenario | Range | incumbent chars | cap x | twins | chunked-bitset chars | vs incumbent | delta-list chars | vs incumbent | u-run-length chars | vs incumbent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|:-:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `uniform-random 1%` | 1,000,000 | 17,579 | 4.3 | yes | 25,110 | -42.8% | 14,094 | +19.8% | 18,658 | -6.1% |
| `uniform-random 5%` | 100,000 | 5,836 | 1.4 | yes | 12,523 | -114.6% | 4,616 | +20.9% | 7,306 | -25.2% |
| `uniform-random 5%` | 1,000,000 | 58,783 | 14.4 | yes | 125,110 | -112.8% | 45,421 | +22.7% | 69,476 | -18.2% |
| `uniform-random 20%` | 100,000 | 11,553 | 2.8 | yes | 11,550 | +0.0% | 12,159 | -5.2% | 19,443 | -68.3% |
| `uniform-random 20%` | 1,000,000 | 114,865 | 28.0 | yes | 114,918 | -0.0% | 126,523 | -10.1% | 189,184 | -64.7% |
| `clustered-bursts` | 1,000,000 | 3,574 | 0.9 | yes | 4,111 | -15.0% | 4,799 | -34.3% | 3,579 | -0.1% |

**Read this table before acting on a verdict.** Two things about it are load-bearing:

1. **5 of the 6 qualifying rows are already PAST the 4,096-char cap, not merely at the 3,072-char
   back-pressure threshold.** Past the cap PC has dropped the payload and blocked the partition
   whichever encoding won, so a percentage on such a row is a percentage of an already-blocked
   commit and buys an operator no headroom on its own. What density is worth in the regime that
   matters is the *engagement point* table above - the range size at which a family starts to
   block at all - and a candidate moves that only in proportion to its margin. KTD5's rule as
   written is applied exactly here; whether a win concentrated this far past the cap satisfies
   its SPIRIT ("real headroom at the point where density matters") is a judgement for whoever
   decides on U4, and this table is what that decision should be made on.
2. **Incumbents and candidates are now measured under the same compression rule.** Both get a zstd
   twin exactly when their own plain form is large enough to be worth compressing (KTD8). The first
   generation of this report gated the incumbents with the old all-or-nothing rule and the candidates
   per encoder, which flattered the candidates on `!` rows; that asymmetry is gone, and every
   qualifying row above was a `yes` row under either rule.

### Why not the RoaringBitmap library (KTD1)

The `chunked-bitset` rows above ARE Roaring's container model, measured on this corpus: its best
qualifying result is **+0.03%** against the incumbent encoders, far short of the **10%**
ship bar above. The design reasoning behind declining the library lives with the code, in the
offsets package javadoc
(`parallel-consumer-core/src/main/java/bz/stub/parallelconsumer/offsets/package-info.java`).
